question.leadin: Answer the following about David Ben-Gurion.
question.text: David Ben-Gurion was the first prime minister of this country. Perhaps the toughest airport security in the world is at Ben-Gurion's namesake airport in this country's city of Tel Aviv.
question.clue: A mass eviction in this country is commemorated on May 15 as Nakba Day, which comes right after this country's commemoration of its independence on May 14, 1948.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about prominent terrorist groups.
swap.text: This group, led by Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, was responsible for the attacks in November 2015 on Paris that killed 130 people.
swap.clue: Brett McGurk is the American special envoy to a coalition against this group.

question.text: This conflict saw Operation Kadesh, an Israeli invasion of the Sinai Peninsula in a combined effort with Britain and France go take the namesake waterway.
question.clue: This conflict was the center of discussions at the Protocol of Sevres after which Charles Keightley initiated Operation Musketeer.

swap.text: Reporters for the American branch of this Qatar-based news network were tear-gassed and had their camera and lighting system taken down by police.

question.text: In 106 CE, the Roman emperor Trajan annexed the Nabatean kingdom in order to protect a road which had linked Alexandria to this city, a center of steel production. It was the capital of the Umayyad Caliphate.
question.clue: It was later annexed into Alexander the Great's empire and lost importance when the government was moved north to Antioch.

swap.text: Norman Schwarzkopf's father helped the CIA train this fantastically evil Iranian secret police force. It had to be retrained to be slightly less effective at killing after the Siahkal massacre.
swap.answerHtml: SAVAK (or Organization of Intelligence and National Security; or Sāzemān-e Ettelā’āt va Amniyat-e Keshvar)
swap.clue: This organization, most of whose early personnel were trained by Norman Schwarzkopf and the CIA. This organization was the first to operate the notorious Evin University.

question.leadin: During a speech, this leader used the code-word "Ferdinand de Lesseps" to signal his soldiers to seize control of one structure.
question.text: Name this leader who succeeded Mohammad Naguib ("na-GHEEB"). This leader's nationalization of one structure in 1956 sparked a crisis that led to the resignation of British Prime Minister Anthony Eden.
question.clue: This leader helped overthrow King Farouk I in 1952 before founding the United Arab Republic in 1958.

swap.text: The Safavid conversion to the Twelver sect of this branch of Islam is the major reason for its prevalence in Iran today. This smaller of the two major branches of Islam holds that Muhammad's rightful successor was Ali.
swap.clue: This second-largest denomination of Islam, after Sunni.

question.leadin: BONUS. Answer the following about 1967 per part.
question.text: This conflict saw Israeli forces take the old city of Jerusalem.
question.clue: At the beginning of this war, one side immediately destroyed over half the air force of another in Operation Focus.

swap.text: An estimated 2000 to 4000 people participated on June 7, 2002, in the first ever organized parade of gays and lesbians in this city, though religious leaders were outraged. For 15 points-name this city in the Middle East.
swap.clue: Abd al-Malik commissioned a shrine in this city that sits along with the al-Aqsa mosque on the site of a building sacked by Sheshonk I after being completed by Solomon.

question.leadin: Events in this city may have led to a retaliatory explosion near the apartment block of Sheikh Mohammad Hussein Fadlallah.
question.text: Name this Middle Eastern city where 241 American servicemen were killed in a 1983 barracks bombing, the deadliest one-day result for the U.S. military since the Tet Offensive.
question.clue: Up to 3,500 civilians were massacred by Kataeb Party militias in the Sabra and Shatila refugee camps in this city after the assassination of Bachir Gemayel ("jem-AY-yill").

swap.text: Most of those in the People's Crusade were slaughtered at the Battle of Civetot by Kilij Arslan, ruler of these Turkic people who took all of Anatolia at the 1071 Battle of Manzikert.
swap.clue: One offshoot of this dynastic group was the Sultanate of Rum.

question.leadin: This group massacred the inhabitants of Dayr Yasin, and in 1946 they bombed Jerusalem's King David Hotel.
question.text: Name this militant underground movement in Palestine composed of right-wing Zionists.
question.clue: Along with an organization called "Lehi," this group was an offshoot of the Hagana and its political wing would later become the Herut, or "Freedom," party.

swap.leadin: Name these dynasties of world history which existed in 1000 A.D.
swap.text: This dynasty was just getting going, after Said ibn Husayn of northern Syria founded it and its fourth ruler Moizz moved the capital to Cairo. It's named for a daughter of the prophet Muhammad.
swap.clue: Turkish general al-Basasiri handed control of Baghdad to this caliphate, but he was later driven out by Seljuks, and the Byzantines ended up driving it out of Sicily.

question.leadin: One member of this ethnic group named Ibn al-'Awwam described the proper cultivation of olive trees in his Book on Agriculture.
question.text: Name these people who spread the sakia water wheel to Spain and revolutionized agriculture between the 8th and 13th centuries. These conquerors of Al-Andalus enlarged the Bahr Yussef canal connecting Fayyum to the Nile.
question.answerHtml: Arabs [or Arab Agricultural Revolution; accept Moors; prompt on Umayyads; or Andalusians; or Egyptians]
question.clue: These people fought on both sides of the Battle of Badr and conquered the Sassanid Empire.

swap.leadin: This man attempted to catch a pair of shoes thrown at George W. Bush during a press conference.
swap.text: Name this former Prime Minister of Iraq whose accession was brokered by Qasem Soleimani as a compromise between Kurds and Shi'ites.

question.leadin: Answer some things about military blunders of the Umayyad Caliphate.
question.text: In this 750 AD battle, an Umayyad army under Marwan II was defeated by an insurgent force of Abbasids under as-Saffah at a tributary of the Tigris. The battle at this river ended the Umayyad dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Battle of the Zab River [or the Great Zab] 10

swap.leadin: Thomas Friedman named a set of "rules" that describes the ethos of the Middle East after this city.
swap.text: Name this Syrian city where 300 people were killed in 1981 by government security forces. A year later, thousands of citizens were brutally murdered in this city as part of the repression of an uprising by the Muslim Brotherhood.

question.text: The Kurdish genocide was codenamed the "campaign" of this eighth sura of the Quran, whose English translation is roughly "the spoils of war."

swap.leadin: Name these things about a Muslim dynasty, FTP each.
swap.text: The rulers of this Sunnite dynasty included Al-Adil and Al-Kamil, the brother and nephew of its founder Saladin.
swap.clue: This dynasty lost territory under al-Adil and al-Kamil, and was finally driven out of its chief territory following the Battle of al-Mansurah.
